yaml.title: DSA261 — Algorithmic Learning and AI
yaml.subtitle: Search. Question. Use AI. Verify. Decide.

markdown.markdown:
::: {.hero-panel}

**Central question:** In an algorithmically mediated world, how do we know what to trust, what to question, and how to use AI to expand our abilities without surrendering judgment?

**TRACE** is the recurring learning protocol of the course:

> **Predict → Encounter → Probe → Explain → Decide → Verify**
:::

## This is a lab-based course

Although DSA261 is formally a three-hour theoretical course, teaching takes place in the computer laboratory. You will search, compare, prompt, interrogate, verify, document evidence, and make decisions every week.

The goal is not passive familiarity with AI terminology. The goal is **observable capability**.

## Week 1 is live

::: {.action-grid}
::: {.action-card}
### Week 1 — How Do You Know?
Information seeking, source tracing, verification, and epistemic agency.

[Open Week 1 TRACE Lab](weeks/week01.qmd){.btn .btn-primary}
:::

::: {.action-card}
### Course Guide
Learn how TRACE, quizzes, weekly Tasks, and evidence work.

[Read the Course Guide](course-guide.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::
:::

## The semester story

1. **How do you know?**
2. **Who shapes what you see?**
3. **What does AI actually do?**
4. **Can AI make you better?**
5. **How can it fail?**
6. **How do you control and verify it?**
7. **Who remains responsible?**
